<div class="nv-rule" id="for-init-clause">

## A `for` init clause is one typed declaration or a list of expressions, never both

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#for-init-clause"><code>iteration/for-init-clause</code></a>
</div>

A `for` header's init clause holds **one typed local declaration, or a list of expressions, and never
a mix**:

```
for-init := local-decl | expr (',' expr)* | ε
```

`local-decl` is the ordinary typed local declaration in full — `int $i = 0`, `var $i = 0`, and any
other type the grammar spells — with exactly one binding and no comma tail. The condition and step
clauses are unchanged and stay expression lists: a step is a reassignment or an increment, both
expressions already, and a declaration there would re-declare on the second iteration.

The declaration form lowers to the same slot store the declare-above form lowers to, at the same
point in the same block, so a counter in the header costs nothing in time or space. Both spellings
work and neither is rewritten into the other; a counter read after its loop, or shared by two loops,
is the case that still wants the declaration above.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#for-counter-scope" title="A header-declared counter is function-scoped, and a second header declaring it again is refused"><code>iteration/for-counter-scope</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#for-init-refusals" title="A refused for header is one diagnostic, never a cascade"><code>iteration/for-init-refusals</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0109.md">record 0109</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0037.md">record 0037</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/a-for-header-declares-its-own-counter.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/a-for-header-declares-its-own-counter.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/a-for-loop-runs-init-condition-and-step.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/a-for-loop-runs-init-condition-and-step.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/tests/stmt.rs"><code>crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/tests/stmt.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="for-counter-scope">

## A header-declared counter is function-scoped, and a second header declaring it again is refused

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#for-counter-scope"><code>iteration/for-counter-scope</code></a>
</div>

A counter declared in a `for` header is **function-scoped**, exactly as every other binding is. It is
readable after the loop, holding the value that ended it, and a second `for` header below it
declaring the same name again is a re-declaration diagnostic naming the first — there is no
shadowing, and the header form is given no scope of its own.

So [`iteration/for-init-clause`](/docs/rules/iteration/#for-init-clause "A for init clause is one typed declaration or a list of expressions, never both") is a spelling change and not a scoping one. The declaration in a
header is the same statement a declaration anywhere else is, which is what makes the declare-once
rule, definite assignment and the lowering all apply to it unchanged.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#for-init-clause" title="A for init clause is one typed declaration or a list of expressions, never both"><code>iteration/for-init-clause</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#for-init-refusals" title="A refused for header is one diagnostic, never a cascade"><code>iteration/for-init-refusals</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0109.md">record 0109</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/a-for-header-declares-its-own-counter.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/a-for-header-declares-its-own-counter.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/a-second-for-header-redeclaring-its-counter-is-refused.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/a-second-for-header-redeclaring-its-counter-is-refused.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-types/src/locals.rs"><code>crates/nvs-types/src/locals.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

<div class="nv-rule" id="for-init-refusals">

## A refused `for` header is one diagnostic, never a cascade

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#for-init-refusals"><code>iteration/for-init-refusals</code></a>
</div>

Two grammatical refusals, each raised once and each naming the spelling that works:

- **`E0124`** — a `for` init clause holds one declaration or a list of expressions, not both. Raised
  where the second item begins, on `for (int $i = 0, $j = 1; …)` and on `for ($j = 1, int $i = 0; …)`
  alike. The help names both fixes: move the extra initialiser above the loop, or make both
  expressions.
- **`E0125`** — a `for` init clause declares at most one binding. Raised on the second declaration of
  `for (int $i = 0, int $j = 0; …)`. Separate from `E0124` because the fix differs: the second
  declaration goes above the loop.

Each refused header reports **one** diagnostic and no second one, and keeps whatever declaration it
held so no later phase reports an undeclared counter on top of it.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#for-init-clause" title="A for init clause is one typed declaration or a list of expressions, never both"><code>iteration/for-init-clause</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#for-counter-scope" title="A header-declared counter is function-scoped, and a second header declaring it again is refused"><code>iteration/for-counter-scope</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0109.md">record 0109</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/a-for-init-clause-is-a-declaration-or-expressions-not-both.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/a-for-init-clause-is-a-declaration-or-expressions-not-both.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/a-for-init-clause-declares-at-most-one-binding.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/a-for-init-clause-declares-at-most-one-binding.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="foreach-subjects">

## `foreach` drives exactly three subjects, and a fourth is refused where it is written

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#foreach-subjects"><code>iteration/foreach-subjects</code></a>
</div>

`foreach` accepts three subjects and refuses a fourth where it is written:

- an **`array<T>`**, iterated directly by the IR with no interface call and no allocation;
- an **`Iterable<T>`**, whose `iterate()` is called once and whose returned cursor the loop drives;
- an **`Iterator<T>`**, driven directly.

Anything else is a compile error at the subject. Only the array form binds a key — a cursor has no
key to give ([`iteration/two-interfaces`](/docs/rules/iteration/#two-interfaces "Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is advance() then current()")), so a key binding over one is refused rather than
filled with a counter, and an array's key binds as a string.

Each of the three gives its value binding the element type `T`, which a written binding type is
checked against and a `var` binding takes as its own ([`types/var-inference`](/docs/rules/types/declarations-and-numbers/#var-inference "var takes a local's or a foreach binding's type from the expression that fills it, and fixes it there for good")).

An object becomes iterable by declaring one of the two interfaces at a concrete type
([`iteration/concrete-generic-implements`](/docs/rules/iteration/#concrete-generic-implements "A class implements a compiler-owned generic interface at a concrete type, and declares no type variable of its own")). There is no other way in: no property walk, and no
interface that turns a subscript or a count into a method call
([`iteration/no-magic-collection-interfaces`](/docs/rules/iteration/#no-magic-collection-interfaces "A class cannot make $obj[$k] or a count into a method call")).

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>An object is iterable only by declaring <code>Iterable&lt;T&gt;</code> or <code>Iterator&lt;T&gt;</code>; walking an ordinary object's public properties does not compile</p>
</aside>

call"><code>iteration/no-magic-collection-interfaces</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#generators" title="A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without <div class="nv-rule" id="two-interfaces">

## Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is `advance()` then `current()`

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#two-interfaces"><code>iteration/two-interfaces</code></a>
</div>

Iteration has exactly two interfaces, both reserved names the compiler owns:

```
interface Iterator<T> {
    public function advance(): bool;   // move to the next element; false once exhausted
    public function current(): T;      // the element advance() just moved to
}

interface Iterable<T> {
    public function iterate(): Iterator<T>;
}
```

`Iterator<T>` is a **single-pass cursor**; `Iterable<T>` is a thing that can hand out a fresh one, so
draining an `Iterable<T>` twice walks it twice and draining an `Iterator<T>` twice does not. The pair
is `advance`-then-`current` rather than one `next(): ?T`, because a single method cannot tell "the
sequence ended" from "the next element is `null`", and Novis has nullable types.

Both members are declared without a body, and a class is held to every one of them. A cursor carries
**no key half** — nothing in `Iterator<T>` produces one — which is why a `foreach` over a cursor may
bind a value and not a key ([`iteration/foreach-subjects`](/docs/rules/iteration/#foreach-subjects "foreach drives exactly three subjects, and a fourth is refused where it is written")).

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>No <code>rewind()</code>, <code>key()</code>, <code>valid()</code> or <code>IteratorAggregate</code>, and none of the ~20 SPL iterator classes; a cursor has two members and no key half</p>
</aside>

<div class="nv-rule" id="concrete-generic-implements">

## A class implements a compiler-owned generic interface at a concrete type, and declares no type variable of its own

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#concrete-generic-implements"><code>iteration/concrete-generic-implements</code></a>
</div>

Type variables belong to declarations the compiler owns. A user class gets one narrow door onto
them: it may **implement a compiler-owned generic interface at a concrete type** —
`implements Iterator<User>`, `implements Iterable<int>` — fixing `T` at the declaration site, where
the argument is recorded on the class's signature and checked against every member body.

That is substitution of one concrete type into a known interface, and nothing more. A class may not
declare a type variable of its own, there is no inference, no variance, and no type-parameter scope
inside the class body. The door exists so a collection can be iterated
([`iteration/two-interfaces`](/docs/rules/iteration/#two-interfaces "Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is advance() then current()")) without opening user-defined generics.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#two-interfaces" title="Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is advance() then current()"><code>iteration/two-interfaces</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#foreach-subjects" title="foreach drives exactly three subjects, and a fourth is refused where it is written"><code>iteration/foreach-subjects</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0053.md">record 0053</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-types/tests/generics.rs"><code>crates/nvs-types/tests/generics.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="no-magic-collection-interfaces">

## A class cannot make `$obj[$k]` or a count into a method call

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#no-magic-collection-interfaces"><code>iteration/no-magic-collection-interfaces</code></a>
</div>

`ArrayAccess` and `Countable` do not exist, and no other interface makes a syntactic form dispatch to
a method. `$obj[$k]` on anything that is not an array does not compile.

A collection exposes ordinary members instead: `->get($k)`, `->set($k, $v)` and `->count()`. Each of
those buys notation at the cost of a call that does not look like one, which is the same implicit
dispatch already rejected for `$obj->prop`; and reading as an array while none of `Core\Arr` applies
is a second cost with no offsetting capability. Iteration is the one place a capability is bought —
streaming a cursor without materialising it — and it has its own interfaces
([`iteration/two-interfaces`](/docs/rules/iteration/#two-interfaces "Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is advance() then current()")).

`nvs convert` has no mechanical path for either interface: each becomes a diagnostic naming the
member that replaces it.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>ArrayAccess</code> and <code>Countable</code> do not exist; a collection exposes <code>-&gt;get($k)</code>, <code>-&gt;set($k, $v)</code> and <code>-&gt;count()</code> instead</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#foreach-subjects" title="foreach drives exactly three subjects, and a fourth is refused where it is written"><code>iteration/foreach-subjects</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#two-interfaces" title="Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is advance() then current()"><code>iteration/two-interfaces</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0053.md">record 0053</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0028.md">record 0028</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0014.md">record 0014</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0011.md">record 0011</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="cursor-out-of-range">

## `current()` outside the protocol throws rather than answering

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#cursor-out-of-range"><code>iteration/cursor-out-of-range</code></a>
</div>

`current()` throws a `LogicError` when it is called before the first `advance()`, and when it is
called after an `advance()` returned `false`. It answers only between those two points:

```
current() outside the iteration protocol: it answers only after advance() returned true
```

There is no sentinel for "outside the sequence" and no third member to ask first — `advance()`'s
`bool` is the whole of the liveness answer ([`iteration/two-interfaces`](/docs/rules/iteration/#two-interfaces "Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is advance() then current()")), so a consumer that
ignores it is asking for an element the cursor does not have. Both points need the guard for the
same reason and neither is the harmless one: before the first `advance()` the slot holds the element
type's null payload, and after the last it still holds the final element, which looks like an answer.

A `foreach` advances and reads in lockstep, so it never stands outside the protocol. A generator's
cursor is guarded at the same two points, and a generator that yields nothing makes them one point.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>Reading a cursor before it has advanced, or after it is drained, is an error rather than a <code>null</code> or a stale element</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#two-interfaces" title="Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is advance() then current()"><code>iteration/two-interfaces</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#generators" title="A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it"><code>iteration/generators</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0053.md">record 0053</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/error/iterator-current-outside-the-protocol-throws.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/error/iterator-current-outside-the-protocol-throws.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="generators">

## A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#generators"><code>iteration/generators</code></a>
</div>

A function whose body contains `yield` is a **generator**. Its declared return type must be
`Iterator<T>`, and every `yield` operand is checked against that `T`. Calling it runs no user code:
it allocates and returns the state object, which implements `Iterator<T>`, and the body then runs one
segment per `advance()`. Two calls to the same method give two cursors that advance independently.

The body is compiled by an explicit **state-machine transform** — split at each `yield` into
resumption states reached through an N-way switch, with every local live across a `yield` parked in
the state object rather than on a stack. A generator is therefore an ordinary object: ten thousand
live ones cost ten thousand small objects, not ten thousand stacks, and suspension stays a property
of I/O rather than of ordinary control flow.

A `finally` the generator is suspended inside still runs when the consumer abandons it, and
definite assignment reasons across resumption edges exactly as it does across a linear body.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A generator is a compiled state machine rather than a suspended stack, so it costs one small object and behaves the same on every compile target</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#yield-lexical-confinement" title="yield appears only in the generator's own body"><code>iteration/yield-lexical-confinement</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#one-way-only" title="A generator is a lazy sequence and nothing more"><code>iteration/one-way-only</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#two-interfaces" title="Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is advance() then current()"><code>iteration/two-interfaces</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#generator-stays-in-one-isolate" title="A generator does not cross a boundary and does not clone"><code>iteration/generator-stays-in-one-isolate</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0053.md">record 0053</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/iter/a-generator-is-drained-lazily.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/iter/a-generator-is-drained-lazily.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/iter/a-generator-yields-in-order.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/iter/a-generator-yields-in-order.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/iter/two-generators-from-one-method-advance-independently.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/iter/two-generators-from-one-method-advance-independently.nvst</code></a> </div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="one-way-only">

## A generator is a lazy sequence and nothing more

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#one-way-only"><code>iteration/one-way-only</code></a>
</div>

A generator is a lazy sequence in one direction. There is no `yield from`, no `send()` into a
generator, no `throw()` into one, and no generator return value to retrieve — a `return expr;` in a
generator body is refused, and so is a keyed `yield`.

`yield from` is a second spelling of the re-yielding loop in
[`iteration/yield-lexical-confinement`](/docs/rules/iteration/#yield-lexical-confinement "yield appears only in the generator's own body"), and it costs O(nesting depth) per element where the loop
costs O(1) — a real if small loss, recorded rather than hidden. `send()` and `throw()` make a
generator a bidirectional coroutine, which is a different feature wearing the same syntax; Novis has
coroutines already and they are not spelled `yield`.

`yield` is a statement, so it produces no value to consume.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>No <code>yield from</code>, no <code>send()</code>, no <code>throw()</code> into a generator, no keyed <code>yield</code>, and no generator return value to retrieve</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#generators" title="A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it"><code>iteration/generators</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#yield-lexical-confinement" title="yield appears only in the generator's own body"><code>iteration/yield-lexical-confinement</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0053.md">record 0053</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0051.md">record 0051</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/a-yield-has-no-key-half.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/a-yield-has-no-key-half.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/a-yield-is-a-statement-not-a-value.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/a-yield-is-a-statement-not-a-value.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/iter/a-generator-drains-another-generator.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/iter/a-generator-drains-another-generator.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/iter/a-generator-has-no-key-to-bind.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/iter/a-generator-has-no-key-to-bind.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="yield-lexical-confinement">

## `yield` appears only in the generator's own body

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#yield-lexical-confinement"><code>iteration/yield-lexical-confinement</code></a>
</div>

`yield` is confined to the generator's own body. A helper function called from a generator cannot
yield into it, and neither can a closure written inside one — a closure has its own body, so a
`yield` there does not make the enclosing method a generator; it is refused.

Where PHP would delegate to a helper, Novis writes the loop out:

```
foreach ($inner as $v) { yield $v; }
```

This is the price of the state-machine lowering ([`iteration/generators`](/docs/rules/iteration/#generators "A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it")): the transform can
split the body it compiles and nothing else, so a suspension point in a frame it did not generate has
nowhere to be recorded.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A helper called from a generator cannot yield into it; delegation is written as a <code>foreach</code> that re-yields</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#generators" title="A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it"><code>iteration/generators</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#one-way-only" title="A generator is a lazy sequence and nothing more"><code>iteration/one-way-only</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0053.md">record 0053</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-types/tests/generators.rs"><code>crates/nvs-types/tests/generators.rs</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-types/tests/closures.rs"><code>crates/nvs-types/tests/closures.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="generator-stays-in-one-isolate">

## A generator does not cross a boundary and does not clone

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#generator-stays-in-one-isolate"><code>iteration/generator-stays-in-one-isolate</code></a>
</div>

A generator object is not serializable, does not cross a `spawn`, `spawn worker` or `spawn script`
boundary, and does not `clone`. Each attempt is the same refusal any value that cannot be copied
soundly already gets.

The state-machine lowering ([`iteration/generators`](/docs/rules/iteration/#generators "A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it")) makes a generator an ordinary object with
ordinary fields, so the refusal is not a representation limit: those fields are a compiler-chosen
encoding of a suspended program point, and resuming that point in another isolate — or in a second
copy inside this one — has no meaning to give.

Not yet enforced: nothing in the runtime's copy or spawn paths refuses a generator today.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/iteration/#generators" title="A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it"><code>iteration/generators</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0053.md">record 0053</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0023.md">record 0023</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>
